title: Extending Decision Predicate Graphs for Comprehensive Explanation of Isolation Forest
summary: The paper addresses the opacity of Isolation Forest by extending Decision Predicate Graphs to provide global explanations of iForest. It converts iForest split rules and training-sample traversals into a weighted directed predicate graph and introduces the Inlier-Outlier Propagation Score (IOP-Score). On Annthyroid, the predicate TSH > receives the lowest IOP-Score, -0.2429, identifying it as the strongest outlier-associated predicate in the reported DPG.

match_target.why: Directly matches the user's target hint and is the paper's central Annthyroid result; it uses the same iForest+DPG computation as any other Annthyroid IOP-Score and is CPU-only and cheap.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: IOP-Score is a bounded score in [-1,1] printed as a decimal, and no repeated-run std is reported; use the 0.02 absolute decimal band rather than a relative band.

requirements.stmt: Use scikit-learn's IsolationForest (or equivalent) with 200 iTrees for the Annthyroid experiment.
requirements.quote: We applied our proposal to obtain an iForest model (using 200 iTrees) into a DPG and obtained results similar to the literature [21].

requirements.stmt: Extract predicates from every internal node of every iTree as triples (f, σ, v), with sign σ in {>, ≤}.
requirements.quote: These predicates are represented as triples (f, σ, v), where the sign (σ) can be either > or ≤.

requirements.stmt: Traverse every training sample through each iTree, record ordered predicate lists, and append the model-assigned Outlier/Inlier label.
requirements.quote: Each list is then extended by appending the label previously assigned to the observations

requirements.stmt: For outlier sets, remove predicate lists whose path length exceeds the tree maximum depth.
requirements.quote: we eliminate all predicate lists that exceed the trees’ maximum depth from the outlier sets.

requirements.stmt: Collapse predicate triples to pairs (f, σ), discarding split values v for cross-tree aggregation.
requirements.quote: we further refine them by removing the values (v) from each predicate triple, resulting in pairs of the form (f, σ).

requirements.stmt: Add a directed edge only when two predicates appear consecutively in a recorded list, preserving order; edge weight is frequency.
requirements.quote: the predicate in the first node is immediately followed by the predicate in the second node

requirements.stmt: Apply class-imbalance weights wo=(No+Ni)/No for outlier transitions and wi=(No+Ni)/Ni for inlier transitions.
requirements.quote: If the instance is classified as an outlier, its contribution to the frequency is multiplied by a weight wo.

requirements.stmt: Compute IOP-Score(v) as the difference between Inlier and Outlier terminal frequencies, normalized by the node context.
requirements.quote: the difference between the frequency of data transitions from a node toward the “Inlier” class and those toward the “Outlier” class

requirements.stmt: Use fin(v) as the denominator term in the IOP-Score normalization.
requirements.quote: fin(v) is the sum of the frequencies of all edges entering node v.

requirements.stmt: Include terminal “Outlier” and “Inlier” nodes connected to predicate nodes based on appended labels.
requirements.quote: The resulting graph shows two classes: “Outlier” and “Inlier”, with their respective predicates distinguished by their frequency and position within the model logic.

requirements.stmt: Use the iForest maximum-depth definition ceil(log2(min(256, |X|))) for depth cutoff.
requirements.quote: The iTree reaches its maximum depth, which is defined as:

requirements.stmt: Use model-predicted Outlier/Inlier labels, not ground-truth anomaly labels, to color/label graph paths.
requirements.quote: These observations are assigned labels: “Outlier” if the model classifies them as such, and “Inlier” otherwise.

requirements.stmt: For Annthyroid, use the six numerical features and 6,916 samples, excluding binary features.
Preserve the Annthyroid class imbalance of 3.61% anomalous samples when computing weights.
requirements.quote: anomalous instances accounting for only 3.61 % of the total samples.

requirements.stmt: Use Graphviz to render the DPG visualization.
requirements.quote: Graphviz enabled the visualization of the DPG2 , enhancing the interpretability of the decision-making process.
